title: Gathering & Gauging
body:
Now that we're floating around the PNW for a few, I thought I'd restructure the site here... This whole site is a journal and I'll break things up into chapters to keep things clean and orderly. Figured now that we've been back here a bit, we'd start a new chapter, and let the southwest adventure stand on its own. 

It's been so nice to see family back here in The Gorge, get some great hugs in, some singing with Grandma and Grandpa Sanders, seeing granny steadily getting back to full health. Time at the giant house with the Big Guy's fam was so nice. Man... it's so lush and green! 

Just got back to Bend to greet the Big Guy's mom and hang with her for a week or so. And then we're not quite sure what... Alaska has been on the menu, but there's also a hankering for stability, and living so frugally and just dumping money on student loans... I know that sounds bland, but the Big Guy figures he might as well while he can... Kinda like the year he took off drinking... maybe he takes a year to just throw money at the pit that's kept him from buying a home for so long. 

Anyway, just with all of this contemplation, wondering, and ruminating... seemed like a good time to start a chapter 2 of this journal. Maybe you all can help nudge us in a good direction in the poll (top menu bar) or with direct messages?! 

I feel like a window sill to call my own might be nice, but so is the road...

body: Just touching base to show that we hit another state - Idaho.

title: Montana
body:
Well... it's been a minute. Almost a month actually now that I pay attention... 

It's been spent recouping in Stevenson Washington with the big guy's parents, But also in Bend Oregon visiting his Mom and all the Palmers there. I've gotten used to the various places we stay at and make sure to cry my ass off incessantly for hours when we leave Granny and Grandpa's. 

What an amazing reset - Mom's Birthday, family fire, croquet, grandparents, friends, hikes, dinners, Terminator movies, Work that the big guy is really proud of (with Dave Chapelle), Chinese checkers, and on and on, amazing and awesome.

We've now made it to Hot Springs Montana to visit his cousin and her amazing family. What a generous and considerate, lively (and a little chilly) change of pace. SO many awesome kiddos, dinners, animals... The heart-filling goodness of a pre-language toddler demanding that you paint with her, and look at the things she's collected in the bottom of the popcorn machine's storage box. Or when her big sister wanders out to the camper just to check on us and give me a few pets.

Maybe sitting and stewing, churning over plans, options, considerations is not the best way to find clarity... Maybe it's better to lighten up, let go and enjoy the company of the amazing people who invite you in. Maybe after some of that, its not so much that the clarity you were after shows up, but more that you realize you don't have time to hunt for clarity when you're having such a good time just being. 

Something to chew on. 

But, when it comes to it, there are still inflection points... do we drive up to Alaska from here, or head back south? Vote in the poll and let us know what you think?

PS - Oh and check out the photos of the big guy when he was real tiny and hanging with my namesake (or me before I came back?)

title: Canadian Cleanse
body:
Just woke up in the truck, parked outside a Ramada in Golden, BC. It's cold and the Big Guy seems rejuvenated (even if he was fairly annoyed with my late-night sad meows and pretty constant self-cleaning). Sounds like he did this trek 3 times before, and that each time it feels like passing through Canada is some kinda emotional or "spiritual" cleansing... (I know, he can be a bit flowery). 

Maybe its the ample hours on the road, reflecting, singing the pixies on repeat, or listening to audiobooks about meditation and anarchy... He seems to think it's to do with the time reflecting on where he's coming from and where he's headed, familiar or fresh. As Dave Matthews said - "See, you and me have it better than most can dream, have it better than the best, so we can pull on through whatever tears at us, whatever holds us down, and if nothing can be done, we'll make the best of what's around. Turns out not where but who you're with that really matters."

If he's learned anything, he's realized that changing places over the years may help his eyes see fresh, but it's never the place that stirs his innards, but the people he finds. Not sure stirring innards sounds appealing, but it's better than a set of stale eyes, I guess. Seems a worthy endeavor to try to remain fresh without having to pass through Canada every few years... But, sounds like he thinks is always a treat. Canada is beautiful and safe, reassuring, welcoming and generous. 

Anyway, he wanted to get us over the border and a decent ways into Canada to eat into the huge roadtrip as much as possible. Hoping to get past Fort Nelson somewhere today, then Tok, Alaska the next, and on to Anchorage the next. 

I've been sad meowing a lot. That camper we stayed in was so very nice, and the cousins who hosted us were just incredible. The singing, smiles, laughs, MEALS, just the generosity and consideration were unparalleled. 

But the Big Guy says its time to press on towards his home while we can, before he gets back to his weird screen-staring job, which is apparently extremely demanding of his time, as of late. 

We'll post more deeply reflective thoughts when I'm not crying and he's not driving!

title: An Epic Day
body:
Raw notes dictated as the Big Guy drove:

2 new hats

9 black bears

2 grizzlies

12 porcupines

1 Fox

3 rabbits

Countless bison, sheep, Caribou, moose

3 provinces

1,117 miles (1,797 kilometers)

19.5 hours

Sacred Mucho Lake
Looping exit and return importance
Baptism - learned from Jerica
Gateway

Lightness
Relief
Comfort
Midnight Sun
Familiarity
Belonging
Found

The greening
New dedication to expand a sense of self in a way that is detrimental
Tons of reflecting on and gratitude for the most recent out

I wanna go to a first tap, salmon, fest, sewer, Fourth of July, solstice at Harding, music in the park downtown, puppies, park strip, coastal Trail, Campbell Creek Trail, flat top, jac Sprat, the sit Mark , Westchester Lagoon , Kalani Brothers ,Mary's cabin… Wow, living elsewhere it was all just put out of my mind.

This isn't meant to be dramatic… Maybe Mucho Lake really is Gateway or maybe I'm mildly delirious and somewhat of a trance after 19 hours of driving… But it really is vivid

One of the most epic days of my life.
